newsitem.title: JAPAN: No power loss seen from Japan reactor shutdown.
newsitem.headline: No power loss seen from Japan reactor shutdown.

text.p: Japanese power utilities said on Wednesday that the shutdown of the Fugen nuclear reactor would have little impact on their operations as the plant supplies only a fraction of their total electricity.

"We don't even count electricity from Fugen when we draw up our supply plans," said a spokesman for Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, one of three firms which buys electricity from the reactor in Fukui prefecture on the Sea of Japan coast.
The 50,000 kilowatt (kw) of electricity Kansai receives from the 165,000 kw advanced thermal reactor is dwarfed by the firm's total capacity of 37 million kw.

The Science and Technology Agency ordered the state-owned Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) to shut down operations at the plant from late on Tuesday after learning that the PNC had delayed reporting a radiation leak.
Chubu Electric Power Co Inc and Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc each receives about 50,000 kw from Fugen, accounting for 0.17 percent and one percent of their total supply capacities, respectively.
The two firms said the shutdown had no substantial impact on their production and supply plans as the loss would be easily covered by raising operating rates at thermal power plants.
In contrast to nuclear reactors, which usually run at a certain rate, the operating rates of thermal power plants are often adjusted to meet changing demands for electricity.
